correctness.rationale: The axial interval is [max_i(c_i−R_i), min_i(c_i+R_i)] with positive length. Its squared section radius f=-z²+g has g the lower envelope of affine functions with slopes 2c_i; it is positive inside and zero at both ends. The effective center C=g′/2 is nonincreasing; duplicate lines and point ties do not contribute. The density of Z is proportional to f^h with h=(d−1)/2 and the transverse conditional variance is f/(d+1) by uniform ball integration, also valid for interval slices at d=2. Thus (f^(h+1))′=(d+1)(C−z)f^h. Multiplying by z−E[Z] and integrating by parts gives the gap −Cov(Z,C(Z)); continuity cancels all inner boundary terms. Expressing C as a constant minus its positive jumps times 1_{Z>t_j} gives the exact interface contributions. Each has positive masses on both sides and strictly ordered conditional means. No jumps force g affine; the two endpoint zeros reconstruct the entire generating ball, and conversely a ball is isotropic. For the stated three-ball example, direct polynomial antiderivatives give ∫f=17/6, ∫z²f=139/240, ∫f²=191/40, and ∫_{1/2}^1 z f=59/192. With centroid zero these yield the stated variances, difference 59/272 and two equal interface terms 59/544. In the wider absolutely continuous profile class the same integration by parts is valid, and a nonconstant a.e. decreasing C gives strictness by independent pairs. The bundled script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The discrete jump representation needs the finite effective envelope; the broader profile observation does not assert finitely many interfaces.
No conclusion about noncollinear centers or nonuniform densities.

value.rationale: The sign and ball rigidity describe a natural class of uniform bodies without assuming a midpoint centroid or even equal radii. More informative than simply integrating sectional geometry, the exact noncancelling formula tells which effective geometric changes generate the anisotropy, and the three-active-ball example demonstrates genuinely additive behavior beyond the known lens case.
residual_risks: No optimum anisotropy at fixed volume or general axis theorem for noncollinear intersections is established.
